cards.explanation: The answer is that they want to know how He got such learning without studying. The Jews ask, “How did this man attain such learning without having studied?” (John 7:15) I think they were looking around for the diploma on the wall, friends. I'd have the same trouble, because my paperwork would say "found in a junk drawer."

The answer is that His teaching comes from the One who sent Him. Jesus says, “My teaching is not My own…” Then He says, “It comes from Him who sent Me.” (John 7:16) The Jews asked about His schooling, and He points past every classroom to the One who sent Him.

The answer is anyone who desires to do God's will. Jesus says, “If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.” (John 7:17) It's about the desire, not the résumé, friends. Anyone can show up with that.

The answer is his own glory. Jesus says, “He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory…” (John 7:18) That's the person who narrates his own highlight reel, bakers. Then Jesus turns it around and talks about the one who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him.

The answer is “Why are you trying to kill Me?” After He says that none of them keeps the law of Moses, Jesus asks exactly that (John 7:19). John had already told us the Jews in Judea were looking for a way to kill Him (John 7:1). This is a heavy moment, friends, and Jesus says it straight out.
The answer is False. The crowd doesn't admit it. They say, “You have a demon…” and then ask, “Who is trying to kill You?” (John 7:20) That's a long way from "yes, it's us," friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says circumcision is “not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.” (John 7:22) Moses was Israel's leader, and he gave them the law. The practice reaches back even before him, bakers.

The answer is well. Jesus asks, “…why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?” (John 7:23) He points out that a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so the law of Moses won't be broken. Then He sets that next to making a whole man well, friends. He asks them to look at the two side by side.
The word is justly. Jesus says, “Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.” (John 7:24) Looks can fool anybody, bakers. Judging justly means looking deeper.

The answer is True. Some people of Jerusalem say, “Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him.” (John 7:26) I bet they found that strange, friends. Then they ask, “Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?”

The answer is that no one will know where the Christ is from. The people say, “But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.” (John 7:27) In their minds, knowing where Jesus is from counts against Him. They talk themselves right out of it, bakers.

The answer is False. Jesus says of the One who sent Him, “You do not know Him, but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.” (John 7:28-29) They know where Jesus is from, friends, but they don't know the One who sent Him.

The answer is that His hour had not yet come. They try to seize Him, but no one lays a hand on Him “…because His hour had not yet come.” (John 7:30) The text gives that as the reason, bakers. Their trying doesn't change it.

The word is signs. Many in the crowd believe in Him and say, “When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?” (John 7:31) They look at what Jesus has done and ask who could do more, friends. That question is theirs, and I think it's a good one.

The answer is that they send officers to arrest Jesus. The Pharisees and the chief priests do exactly that (John 7:32). The crowd whispers, and the leaders answer with officers, friends. That's a big reply to a whisper!
The answer is False. Jesus says, “You will look for Me, but you will not find Me…” He also says, “…where I am, you cannot come.” (John 7:34) The looking is in there, bakers, but the finding is not.

The answer is that they guess He will go to the Jews scattered among the Greeks. The Jews ask, “Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?” (John 7:35) That's their guess, and it comes right after Jesus says He is going to the One who sent Him (John 7:33). They're puzzling over His words, friends, and they say so themselves in verse 36.
